subject: Polity
description: ECI structure, powers, CEC, landmark reforms

questions.stem: The Election Commission of India is established by which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Art 324 — superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, state legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President is vested in the Election Commission. Art 320 deals with the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC). Art 356 — President's Rule in states. Art 370 — the (now-abrogated) special status of J&K.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Chief Election Commissioner of India is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: The President appoints the CEC and Election Commissioners. The 2023 CEC and ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act brought them in on the advice of a three-member panel comprising the PM, the Leader of the Opposition (or leader of the largest opposition party) and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM. Tenure — 6 years or till the age of 65, whichever is earlier.

questions.stem: The Election Commission currently consists of how many members?
questions.explanation: Since 1993, the ECI has been a three-member body — one Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners. It was a single-member body until 1989, briefly made three-member in 1989, dissolved, and restored to three members in 1993. Decisions are taken by majority. T. N. Seshan (CEC 1990-96) is credited with asserting its independence.

questions.stem: The 'NOTA' (None of the Above) option on Indian electronic voting machines was introduced on the directive of the Supreme Court in:
questions.explanation: In PUCL v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court directed the ECI to provide a NOTA option, guaranteeing voter secrecy even for those rejecting all candidates. First used in the 2013 state assembly elections of Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, MP, Rajasthan and Delhi. NOTA does not count towards any candidate; the candidate with the most valid votes still wins even if NOTA leads.

questions.stem: The minimum voting age in India was lowered from 21 to 18 by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: 61st Amendment (1988), effective from March 1989, lowered the voting age from 21 to 18. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'socialist, secular, integrity' to the Preamble and the Fundamental Duties. The 73rd (1992) gave panchayats constitutional status. The 86th (2002) made free compulsory education a Fundamental Right (Art 21A).

questions.stem: A Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner as a judge of the:
questions.explanation: Art 324(5) — the CEC can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds prescribed for a Supreme Court judge — proved misbehaviour or incapacity, by a resolution passed by both Houses with the special two-thirds majority. This insulates the CEC's office from day-to-day political pressure. The other two ECs can be removed on the CEC's recommendation (providing lower protection).

questions.stem: EVMs — electronic voting machines — were used for the first time in all parliamentary constituencies of India in the general election of:
questions.explanation: EVMs were first trialled in a Kerala by-poll in 1982 (Paravur). They were used in phased roll-outs from 1998 onwards, and the 2004 general election was the first to use EVMs in all 543 Lok Sabha constituencies. VVPAT (Voter-Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) slips were rolled out nationally in the 2019 general election.
